subject: AWS Marketplace list-price bypass / channel netting clarifications
messages:
From: Claire Dunn <claire@healthlytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@healthlytics.com
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace pricing question + SKU mapping

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — HealthLytics liked the latency profile and the VPC options. Procurement asked us to check a couple of things before we move to an official PO:

- We need to understand if Redwood can put a private offer on AWS Marketplace that lists the public list price but routes net revenue differently (i.e., we want the customer invoice to reflect list price for our internal finance rules, while channel passback/commissioning follows a different netting). Is that supported, or does AWS block list-price bypass for private offers?

- Second, can Redwood support a bundled SKU (platform + private data connector) on the private offer, where the connector is a reimbursable 3rd-party add-on and should not be subject to the same reseller passback?

Procurement attached a short PO template and a rough SKU mapping that shows how HealthLytics would like the invoice to look (attached: sku_mapping_draft.xlsx). If you can point us to the constraints and a recommended pattern for channel margin handling on Marketplace private offers, that would help accelerate the PO.

Would you and someone from channel ops be available for a 30-min call tomorrow?

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Dunn
Head of Procurement
HealthLytics

Attachments: sku_mapping_draft.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dunn <claire@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace pricing question + SKU mapping

Hi Claire — really appreciate the clear ask and the sketch.

Short answers up front:
- AWS allows private offers with flexible billing presentations, but list-price visibility and how passbacks are applied can be constrained by the marketplace listing and the pricing structure. There are a few patterns we use depending on tax/invoice requirements.
- Bundles are fine, but separating passback treatment (e.g., excluding the connector) usually requires either:
  1) two SKUs on the private offer (primary platform SKU + connector SKU) with the connector marked as reimbursable, or
  2) a bundled SKU with a controlled internal passback waterfall we enforce off-marketplace after settlement.

I attached a short sketch (healthlytics_po_draft.pdf) that maps out the two patterns and the implications for reseller commissions and netting. Quick clarifying questions before I loop Channel Ops:
- Do you need the customer-facing invoice to show the connector as a separately line-item (for reimbursement), or is a single line bundle acceptable as long as Finance can reconcile internally?
- What is your ideal reseller commission percentage on the platform portion (ballpark is fine)? We ask because the passback mechanics change if you need to split by net vs list.

If you can reply to those two bullets I’ll pull Ben and Laura into a short call to finalize the approach and confirm any Marketplace constraints we need AWS to approve.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Kimberly Park
Director, Marketplace Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: healthlytics_po_draft.pdf (1 page pricing sketch)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace pricing question + SKU mapping (internal)

Kimberly / Laura — internal note on channel margin mechanics for HealthLytics:

- If they want invoice to show list price but our net revenue to be lower (so partner commission is calculated on net), we should prefer two-SKU model on AWS: public list SKU (customer-facing) + internal reimbursement SKU that we settle off-marketplace. That keeps AWS invoicing neat and gives Finance the separate lines they want.
- Two risks: 1) AWS charging fees on both SKUs (we need to model the fee double-count effect), 2) more complex settlement with partners.
- If customer insists on a single line bundle on the invoice, passback must be handled by us post-settlement via reverse invoice/credit to reseller (adds latency).

Recommended ask for call: confirm the connector must be line-itemized AND confirm the expected reseller commission (if they say ~15% we can propose a netting waterfall).

I'll prep a short slide for the call that shows fee impact (AWS fee assumptions + reseller passback). Laura — can you validate latest fee percentages I used (AWS marketplace fee 6% platform + 2% transaction) and whether Finance is ok with off-marketplace reimbursement flows?

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Channel Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dunn <claire@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace pricing question + SKU mapping

Hi Claire — quick follow-up with the two recommended patterns and the pros/cons (see inline). I also attached the draft PO language that maps to each approach.

Pattern A — Two-SKU private offer (recommended if connector must be line-itemized):
- Listing: platform SKU (list price shown), connector SKU (zeroed or reimbursable line)
- Pros: invoice shows separate lines for Finance/reimbursement; easier to reconcile; minimal off-marketplace settlements.
- Cons: AWS fees may apply separately; need to model fee double-counting.

Pattern B — Single bundled SKU + off-marketplace passback (recommended if customer wants simplest UI):
- Listing: one bundle SKU with total list price. Post-settlement we issue partner credits/adjustments to effect reseller passback on the platform portion only.
- Pros: cleaner customer invoice; fewer SKUs to manage.
- Cons: adds settlement latency and requires partner/Finance coordination.

Action items for our call:
1) Claire to confirm whether the connector must appear as separate line on the invoice.
2) Claire to confirm expected reseller commission % (or range).
3) Kimberly/Ben/Laura to share a one-pager modeling net revenue, AWS fees, and partner passback for each pattern.

Proposed times for 30-min call: Thu 3/5 at 11:00 AM PT or 3:30 PM PT. We can also do Friday morning if that works better.

Attachment: healthlytics_po_draft.pdf (updated, includes PO language mapping)

—
Kimberly Park
Director, Marketplace Sales
Redwood Inference
